newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end up, S&P at high close.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end up, S&P at high close.

text.p: June 10 - U.S. stock index futures ended higher, June S&P 500s ended at new record settlement, below all-time price peak set in morning. Some said futures rise occurred on good volume as orders flowed in late so as not to miss rally. Some said tone felt euphoric, suggesting more but limited upside. Drops in NASDAQ, airline stocks, weak bonds seen limiting gains.

A soft close in U.S. Treasury bond futures, which eroded from small morning gains, briefly weighed on stock futures. But once that pressure subsided, brokers said buyers ventured in again and returned June futures to moderate daily gains.
The Dow 30 stock average also hurdled the 7,500 level, very roughly equal to the 865.00 level in June S&P 500 futures, which further enflamed buyers during the final 15 minutes.
The revitalized buying at the close wiped out tiny losses that spilled over from a drop in over-the-counter issues plus declines in airline stocks that slammed transportation indices lower.
Those pressures had shoved stock index futures back down toward the minus side following an explosive morning rally.

June S&P 500s had flirted with the downside at the opening bell but then mustered enough dealer buying to cause locals to cover shorts and hit buy stops as OTC stocks temporarily shook off weakness and advanced, floor brokers said.
The futures contract sailed above resistance near 870.00, drawing more buying until it topped out for the day at 872.25, well above the previous record high of 867.20 set yesterday.
Although some professionals were eyeing rallies as potential sales, few were willing to step out aggressively.
They still voiced concern, however, that the market may have become bloated with buyers, possibly signaling the beginning of an end to this leg of the rally.

"The market's very euphoric, so there isn't that much (in futures) for sale," the broker added. "It feels like a meltup...I think they trade up to 890 or 900. That's not that far away. Euphoria indicates the end of the move."

June S&P 500s rose 2.85 pts to 868.70, Value Lines rose 1.40 to 771.70, Nikkei rose 275.0 to 20,545.0, Midcap added 0.70 to 283.75, NYSE Composite rose 1.85 to 453.20, Russell lost 0.25 to 390.0, and NASDAQ fell 12.95 to 944.25.
